claims.description: Problem 1 (1st-order ODE): With Psi_t = 1 + x*N(x,p), 10 hidden sigmoids and 10 collocation points, achieve high accuracy (max error ~1e-6 to 1e-5) over [0,1].
claims.measured: 10 collocation points, 10 hidden units; max |err| on 200-point grid = 2.717e-05; RMSE = 1.513e-05; residual^2 loss = 4.097e-07.
claims.paper_expected: Figure 2 indicates |err| ~ 1e-6 to 1e-5 with 10 hidden units and 10 grid points; high accuracy across the interval.
claims.agreement_comment: Max error is ~2.7e-05, slightly above 1e-5 but same order of magnitude; overall consistent with the paper’s claimed accuracy.

claims.description: Problem 3 (2nd-order BVP): With Psi_t = x sin(1) e^{-1/5} + x(1-x) N(x,p), 10 hidden units and 10 collocation points, achieve max error in the 1e-6 to 1e-5 range.
claims.measured: 10 collocation points, 10 hidden units; max |err| on 200-point grid = 3.543e-06; RMSE = 1.968e-06; residual^2 loss = 3.170e-07.
claims.paper_expected: Figure 5 shows max deviations in the 1e-6 to 1e-5 range for this setup.
claims.agreement_comment: Measured max error is 3.5e-06, well within the reported range; strong agreement.

claims.description: Problem 5 (2D Poisson): With Psi_t = A(x,y) + x(1-x)y(1-y)N(x,y,p), 10x10 grid and 10 hidden units, neural method achieves max deviation ~5e-7 at training and similar at interpolation/test points.
claims.measured: 10x10 training grid, 10 hidden units; max |err| on 41x41 evaluation grid = 9.588e-07; RMSE = 3.470e-07; residual^2 loss = 2.706e-07.
claims.paper_expected: Table 1: NEURAL max deviation ~5e-7 at training and ~5e-7 on a 30x30 test set.
claims.agreement_comment: Max error ~9.6e-07 vs expected ~5e-7; within a factor of ~2 and the same order of magnitude; consistent with the paper’s claim of similar training/test error.

claims.description: Interpolation superiority: neural method has interpolation error comparable to training, while classical discretizations (FEM/FD) are much worse away from training nodes.
claims.measured: On Problem 1: FD (trapezoid) max err at training = 7.989e-04; after cubic-spline interpolation, max err on dense grid = 1.864e-03. ANN max err on same dense grid = 2.717e-05; ANN better than FD-cspline by 68.6x.
claims.paper_expected: Neural method shows excellent interpolation accuracy with deviations at training and interpolation points comparable; FEM shows interpolation errors orders of magnitude larger than at training (e.g., 2e-8 vs 1.5e-5 in Table 1).
claims.agreement_comment: Results support the qualitative claim that ANN interpolation accuracy is superior to a traditional discretization plus interpolation. While the FD training-to-interpolation degradation in this ODE test is not orders of magnitude, ANN is vastly better at off-grid points, aligning with the paper’s qualitative conclusion.

verdict_justification: All three core numerical examples (C1–C3) match the paper’s accuracy claims within the same order of magnitude, and the interpolation superiority (C4) is qualitatively supported by a strong advantage over a traditional method at off-grid points.
